The only editor flags were the known false positive from the in-footnote widget's spacer still carrying data-lw-wraps; fix 5 removes it. On phones, and wherever nothing wraps, nothing changes. Number 1 next to a widget that opens a footnote lines up with the widget's top edge, so nothing is stranded. Sidenotes beside a right widget keep about 60px clear. The CSS can't affect posts without widgets: every selector needs .lwFloatedWidget or [data-lw-wraps], or sits inside .footnote-content. .footnotes also covers the legacy section.footnotes, and the markdown-it hr.footnotes-sep is already hidden, so no second rule appears. hasCollapsedFootnotes is false, and its div.footnotes would still match.

B and C look clearly worse to a reader. B leaves a narrow footnote column beside an empty area under the widget. C loses the hanging indent and puts the numbers about 19px from the widget (/Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/footnotes/b-flowroot/post-1440-fs-left33-direct-long.png, /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/footnotes/c-flow/post-1440-fs-left33-direct-long.png). A's cost is the empty space beside a last widget that has little text after it. That space looks the same as a widget ending a post with no footnotes, so it is acceptable.

Cross-group caution: the reader and editor rules only clear widgets floated at the top level (siblings of the footnotes). If another group lets a widget float inside a quote, list or collapsible and that float spills out of the container, the footnotes will not clear it. That only matters if containers do not choose full width inside.

Also worth noting: with fix 7, each nested widget also runs as a second live iframe in its sidenote, and a third in hover previews. A stateful widget could drift out of step across them.

design:quote.baseline:
Exp 2 code, no new CSS. A blockquote is display:block with padding 16px on all sides and a 3px grey300 left border (createThemeDefaults.ts:180-188, applied by stylePiping.ts:611-615 in both views). It is not its own formatting context, so its box runs under a floated widget and only its lines get shorter.
LEFT widget (every width where it wraps, both views): the quote's bar and its 16px left padding sit under the widget. Beside the widget, the quote text starts 32px from the widget with no bar and no indent, so it reads as plain text. The bar shows above the widget's top edge and again below its bottom, and it shows through the transparent widget along its left edge, so the widget looks like it is inside the quote (baseline/post-1440-q-left33-long.png, post-1440-q-left33-short.png). Bottom aligned: the bar runs down to the widget's top, then disappears beside it.
RIGHT widget: only the quote's empty right padding goes under the widget. The bar stays visible and the text wraps like a paragraph. It looks fine, but the harness flags the box.
Metrics: one box overlap (BLOCKQUOTE) for every quote section at every wrapping width (1440 to 640, 599, 560), in both views. No horizontal scroll at any width. At 622, 600 and 520 and below, no widget wraps and nothing changes.
WIDGET INSIDE A QUOTE: the editor floats it inside the quote, sized against the ROOT column, and it hangs out of a short quote's bottom into the next paragraph (baseline/editor-1440-q-nested-right.png). The reader DROPS it completely: the nested empty div.iframe-widget is not a root block, and ContentItemBody.tsx:495-500 renders <div {...attribs}/> without the HydratedIframeWidget. So the widget vanishes from published posts and from the Post tab (baseline/post-1440-q-nested-left.png).
DIALOGUE (reader only): the absolutely positioned name header (static left = the box's left edge) is drawn ON TOP of a left widget: "Alice" over its top-left corner, "Bob" over its bottom-left (2 text overlaps at 682-wide columns, 1 at 512-573; baseline/post-1440-dlg-left33.png). design:quote.rationale: The only real problem in this group is a quote's bar and indent going under a LEFT widget (and showing through it, since widgets are transparent). Box beside fixes that with the simplest primitive, one rule for both sides. Its 300px fallback is the same threshold as the text wrap rule, and it matches what code blocks (overflow-x:auto) and spoiler blocks (overflow:auto) already do beside floats, so every bordered or backgrounded box in a post behaves the same way. It leaves the author free: a widget can still sit beside any quote, and the editor shows exactly what readers get, so a long quote that looks too narrow beside a 50% widget is visible and fixable by moving the widget. Clearing (C) takes that freedom away, leaves widgets standing alone beside blank space, and breaks bottom alignment (runaway push). The stepped bar (E) turns one quote into what reads as two and breaks list markers. For a widget inside a quote, containing it and measuring it against the quote is the same wrap rule applied to the quote's own column. It looks like a quoted figure and needs no special case, whereas forcing full width would remove a placement that looks fine. Dialogue sections never coexist with widgets, so no rule is forced there.

rejected.name: A: no change
rejected.why: Beside a left widget the quote's bar runs under the transparent widget and the quote text has no bar or indent (box overlap in every quote section at every wrapping width).

rejected.name: C: clears below
rejected.why: Leaves the widget alone with blank space beside it whenever a quote follows it (even a one-line quote). The author can never put a widget beside a quote. align=bottom before a cleared quote runs away (the widget is pushed about 600px down, and further on every edit or resize). It would need extra JS to forbid that.

rejected.name: E: bar follows the text (per-child boxes)
rejected.why: The bar steps sideways between paragraphs, so the quote reads as two quotes. List markers sit on the bar. A single long paragraph is still narrow. It restyles every child block type inside quotes, which is fragile.

rejected.name: D: box beside only after LEFT widgets (not rendered: its look is B on the left plus A on the right, both seen)
rejected.why: CSS ~ cannot tell which widget is nearest, so after any left widget every later quote becomes a box, even beside right widgets. Making it exact needs JS that marks quotes beside a left float. It also makes quotes behave differently by side, while code blocks are boxes on both sides.

rejected.name: Widget inside a quote always shows full width
rejected.why: Simpler JS, but it removes a placement that looks good (a quoted figure with the quote's text wrapping around it). Measuring the same rule against the quote's text width is just as easy to explain.

design:quote.openIssues:
1. Long quote beside a wide widget: a box keeps its narrow width for its whole height. A long quote beside a 50% widget at the 682 column gets about 270px of text and a tall blank strip under the widget (final/post-1440-q-left50-para.png); the same happens beside a right widget. This is the same trade-off code blocks already make. The author sees it in the editor and can move the widget. If Ronny dislikes it, the knob is a larger quote min-width (e.g. 400px border box), which would put quotes below 38% and 50% widgets, but that is a second magic number.
2. Bottom-aligned widget before a long quote: the space above the widget stays blank, because shape-outside lets lines through but not boxes (final/editor-599-q-left33-bottom.png). It is consistent but less useful than with paragraphs. Hiding the bottom option over box-beside blocks would be optional.
3. Widget inside a quote: needs the three JS changes (ContentItemBody render fix, reader content-box width, editor parent width). It was verified only in the editor, which still uses the root column, so the prototype is slightly wider than the final rule (at a 560 window it showed 291px of quote text; 302px after the fix). A 50% widget never wraps inside a quote at the normal 682 column.
4. Found while testing C (not this group's code): any block that clears floats, e.g. a heading, can be the bottom-align target through the gear (CONTEXT 3.4 item 5). That gives the same runaway push seen in c-clear/post-1440-q-right33-bottom-short.png. Worth a guard in alignFloatBottom or the gear.
5. The shared harness /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/proto-render.mjs captures sections lower on the page with blank widgets (iframes outside the viewport are not painted in a full-page capture). Other designers may misjudge from those shots; my render.mjs scrolls each section into view first.
6. Dialogue: no rule, because widgets and dialogue sections cannot be in the same post. Adding '.iframe-widget:has(> .lwFloatedWidget) ~ .dialogue-message' to the same flow-root rule is a one-line safety net if that ever changes.

When a floated widget is still beside the place where the footnotes begin (the widget is the last block, or the text after it is shorter than the widget), the footnotes' 1px top rule runs right through the widget. design:footnotes.rationale: Footnotes are end matter, so they should start under a widget, not wrap around it. "Clears below" is the simplest rule, it matches how headings already behave, and the Exp 2 editor already does it, so the reader just catches up. It gave zero overlaps at all 15 widths in both views. Because it only acts while a widget really floats, it needs no width-specific cases and does nothing to posts without widgets. The author keeps full freedom: the widget stays where it was put, and Bottom alignment (with a paragraph after it) still closes the gap beside it. The only other changes are bug fixes that any choice needs: the bottom-align runaway before a clearing block, and nested widgets that the post page drops. For a widget inside a footnote, full width is the simplest rule and looks fine at every width. Floating it inside the footnote needs the editor to measure the footnote's own width (today the editor and reader disagree) and to apply the 300px rule against a narrower box, which is a lot of machinery for a rare case. Markers and sidenotes already behave well, so per Ronny's rule nothing is forced on them.

design:dividers.baseline: Horizontal rule: Chromium gives hr overflow:hidden and LessWrong's hrStyles make it display:flex with width:100%, so it is its own formatting context that cannot fit beside a float. It already lands below every floated widget (an implicit clear), dots centred on the full column, 16px under the widget's box (the float's bottom margin; the hr's 32px top margin is swallowed). Measured at all 15 widths in both views: never beside a widget, no overlaps, no sideways scroll. So it looks right today. Problems: (1) Bottom-align runaway, a real bug. A widget set to align=bottom whose next block is a divider gets pushed down without limit, because the divider moves down with it and alignFloatBottom keeps chasing it, starting each time from the last push. Measured section heights for that case: Post tab 1243 to 3395px (normal is about 400), editor 2363 to 12653px, growing with every realignment. It leaves a huge empty gap, and in the editor it also shifted every later section between measuring and screenshotting. (2) The editor's drag code reads computed `clear`, which is 'none' for hr, so it treats a divider as an ordinary block. It offers the slot just above a divider (the widget then sits beside nothing) and offers bottom alignment over a divider, which triggers (1). Page break: in the editor (pasted HTML only) it is a full-column 2px grey dashed band with no formatting context, so it runs under a floated widget. The widget is clear (no background), so the band shows through it: harness reported box:FIGURE overlap at every wrapping width. Readers of a saved post get an empty, invisible <figure>. The Exp 3 Post tab renders unsanitized edits, so there it looks like the editor. Harness note: the shared proto-render.mjs screenshots without scrolling, so Chrome does not paint offscreen (cross-origin, throttled) widget iframes and widgets came out blank. My copy /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/design/dividers/render.mjs scrolls each section into view first and also records each divider's box, centre and whether it sits beside a widget.

design:dividers.rationale: A divider is an unnamed section break, so it should behave like the other section break, the heading: the widget stays in the section where the author placed it, and the divider and next section start below it. That is already how it looks today (the 100%-wide flex hr cannot fit beside a float), so the visible change is zero. The real work is making it explicit so the editor's drag geometry and bottom alignment know about it, which fixes a runaway bottom-align bug and dead drop slots. B also leaves the author free: what you put before the divider stays above it, and a widget you want beside the next section goes after the divider. C and D look tidier only when the text before the divider is short. Both make a widget placed at the end of one section visually span the next (with a divider right after the widget, the dots sit level with its top), and D gets cramped between opposite widgets. For the page break, the only visible issue is its grey band showing through the clear widget in the editor. Narrowing it fixes that without changing layout, which keeps the editor matched to readers, who never see a page break. Clearing it would push editor text down where the reader's empty figure does not.

design:lists.baseline:
Lists flow beside floats like paragraphs. Nothing ever overlaps a widget (0 overlaps, no sideways scroll at any width), and lists next to RIGHT widgets are fine: their lines just get shorter. Next to a LEFT widget there are four problems:
(1) Indentation collapses. The list's 40px padding lies under the widget, so item text starts at the widget's text edge (level with the paragraphs there). Chrome puts the outside marker in the 32px gap. Every nested level also starts at that same x, so beside the widget a 3-level list (1. / a. / i.) or (disc / circle / square) is one flat column and only the marker shapes hint at the structure (final/base/editor-800-L50-nested-ol.png).
(2) An item that starts beside the widget and runs past its bottom jumps back to the column indent for its later lines, so the hanging indent breaks.
(3) Markers crowd the widget. Bullets sit 20px from its edge, 1-digit numbers 14px, and 2-digit numbers ("10.") about 5px (they look like they touch it). 3-digit numbers would overlap it.
(4) A real bug with a bottom-aligned left widget whose aligned block is a list. Bottom-align uses margin-top plus shape-outside, and Chrome lays the TEXT out against the shape (full width above the widget) but places outside MARKERS against the float's margin box. So bullets above the widget are drawn in the middle of the text ("enou•gh", "m•odel") and a short item's bullet floats far from its text. This happens in both the editor and the Post tab (final/base/post-1440-L33-bottom-ul.png). The overlap metric does not catch it (it is marker over text, not over the widget).
Checklists look like plain bulleted lists in both views (no checkbox CSS exists anywhere), so they behave exactly like bulleted lists.
A widget inside a list item: the editor floats it inside the item, and it then leaks into the next items and the following paragraph. The Post tab shows nothing there.

candidates.name: A. No change (flows beside)
candidates.description: Today's behavior: lines of list items shorten beside the float; outside markers follow the shortened line in Chrome.
candidates.pros: Nothing to build; right widgets already fine; long lists get full width below the widget.
candidates.cons: Left widget: indent and all nesting levels collapse to one x; long items' wrapped lines jump under the widget; 2-digit numbers 5px from the widget; bottom-aligned left widget beside a list draws bullets over the text (real bug).
candidates.metrics: 0 text/box overlaps, no hscroll at 1440-320; marker gaps to a left widget: bullets 20px, '1.' 14px, '10.' 5px (both views, every wrapping width). Bottom-aligned markers-over-text not counted by the metric.

candidates.name: B. List box beside (ul/ol display: flow-root)
candidates.description: Each root-level list after a floated widget is its own formatting context: the whole list sits beside the widget as one narrower box with its own 40px indent and markers.
candidates.pros: Keeps the indent and nesting beside a left widget; markers 45-60px clear of the widget; fixes the bottom-aligned bug; one clean left edge.
candidates.cons: The list keeps the narrow width for its WHOLE length: a 12-item list after a 50% widget leaves half the column empty below the widget. After a right widget it only costs space (whole list narrow). Would need to be left-only, which needs a side flag in code.
candidates.metrics: 0 overlaps, no hscroll; marker gaps 45-60px; sections up to 104px taller at 800/599 (long lists stay narrow).

candidates.name: C. Item boxes, indent moved onto each item's padding (E = same, left widgets only)
candidates.description: ul padding 0; every li is display: flow-root list-item with padding-inline-start 40px, aiming to keep the indent measured from the widget edge.
candidates.pros: Items below the widget would get the full width back.
candidates.cons: Broken: Chrome draws the outside marker outside the item's border box, so every bullet sits 40px away from its text, beside the widget and everywhere else after it. Visibly changes every list after a widget.
candidates.metrics: 0 overlaps; marker-gap metric says 45-60px, but it assumes the marker hugs the text, which is false here (screenshots show it 40px from its text).

candidates.name: D. Item boxes beside (li display: flow-root list-item)
candidates.description: Every item of a list after a floated widget is its own formatting context; the list keeps its normal 40px padding. Beside a left widget an item's box starts at the widget's text edge (like a paragraph), marker in the gap; below the widget items are back at the normal indent with full width.
candidates.pros: Nested levels keep their indents relative to their parent item; an item's wrapped lines keep one left edge; long lists get full width below the widget; fixes the bottom-aligned bullets-over-text bug; layout with no widget beside it is pixel-identical (same section heights at every non-wrapping width); right widgets unchanged except a straddling item keeps its shorter lines.
candidates.cons: Top-level indent beside a left widget still equals paragraphs there; 2-digit numbers still about 5px from the widget (3-digit would touch it). A bottom-aligned left widget beside a list leaves the space above the widget empty (items avoid the widget's whole margin box).
candidates.metrics: 0 overlaps, no hscroll at all 15 widths, both views; marker gaps same as A (20 / 14 / 5px); heights identical to baseline at 622, 600, 520, 480, 400, 360, 320 (no wraps) and +26 to +78px only where items keep their indents.

candidates.name: H. D plus the indent as each item's left margin
candidates.description: ul padding 0, top-level li flow-root with margin-inline-start 40px, hoping the browser keeps the margin beside the float so the item keeps a 40px indent from the widget edge.
candidates.pros: Would have been the ideal (InDesign-style indent from the wrap edge) if the margin counted.
candidates.cons: Chrome places the box's border edge at the float's margin edge and swallows the margin, so it renders identically to D; other engines may differ, so it only adds cross-browser risk.
candidates.metrics: Identical marker gaps to D (20 / 14 / 5px) at all 15 widths; 0 overlaps; no hscroll.

design:lists.chosen: D. Item boxes beside (li display: flow-root list-item)

design:lists.rationale: D is the smallest rule that fixes every real list problem I saw. The rule: every list item after a floated widget is its own box. It fixes the flattened nested lists and the broken hanging indent beside left widgets, and the bullets drawn over text beside a bottom-aligned left widget. It also keeps long lists using the full width below the widget, and it leaves every list that is not beside a widget pixel-identical: section heights match the baseline exactly at all 7 non-wrapping widths in both views, and right-widget sections match at 1440/800/599. It is one CSS rule (plus a margin fix) for the editor and the reader, needs no JS, and works for both sides. The one cost on the right side is that a straddling item keeps a slightly shorter last line, which reads naturally (sheets/fin-r33pul.png). B (the whole list as a box) looks tidier for short lists, and its markers are further from the widget. But it makes long lists stay narrow for their whole length and would need a left-only flag. C failed because Chrome puts the marker outside the item's border box. H showed Chrome ignores a box's margin beside a float, so the indent from the widget edge cannot be kept with CSS alone. The leftover weakness of D (2-digit numbers about 5px from a left widget) also exists today and is not made worse.

rejected.name: A. No change
rejected.why: Nested lists lose all visible structure beside a left widget. Wrapped lines of a straddling item jump under the widget. A bottom-aligned left widget beside a list draws bullets in the middle of the text (a real bug in both views).

rejected.name: B. List box beside
rejected.why: A long list stays narrow for its whole length (a 12-item list after a 50% widget leaves half the column empty). After a right widget it wastes space for no gain, so it would need a left-only side flag in code. D gets the structural fixes without that cost.

rejected.name: C / E. Item boxes with the indent as item padding
rejected.why: Chrome draws outside markers outside the item's border box, so every bullet ended up 40px from its text, also below the widget.

rejected.name: H. Item boxes with the indent as item margin
rejected.why: Chrome ignores a formatting-context box's margin beside a float, so it renders identically to D; other engines may honor the margin, so it adds cross-browser differences for nothing.

design:lists.openIssues:
1. Two-digit numbers beside a LEFT widget sit about 5px from it and three-digit numbers would reach it, today and with the choice. A pure-CSS fix is not available (Chrome ignores an item box's margin beside a float); the alternative is B (whole list as a box) for numbered lists only, or a wider gutter for lists. 2. Pre-existing, not list-specific: the editor places a floated widget about 18px higher relative to the next block than the Post tab does. The next block starts 12px below the widget's top in the editor and 6px above it in the Post tab, at 1440/800/599, for every section (offset probe: /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/lists/final/final/offsets-*.json). With item boxes, this can change which item first fits beside the widget (L50-nested-ol: item 3 is beside the widget in the post, below it in the editor). Likely the editor's caret sentinel paragraphs or margins around the spacer. 3. Pre-existing: in the editor a nested list sits in its own wrapper item, which adds about 6.5px above each nested level that the reader does not have (visible in nested sheets, baseline too). 4. Post tab: a widget inside a list item renders as an empty `
` (the editor shows it); cause not investigated. The editor UI cannot create this case. 5. Splitting a numbered list by inserting a widget restarts the second half at 1 (code reading; JS fix proposed above). 6. `display: flow-root list-item` falls back to today's behavior in a browser without two-keyword display. Safari and Firefox were not rendered: Firefox historically draws outside markers under a left float, which item boxes should also fix, but this is unverified. 7. Markdown-it posts with loose lists (`

  • `) after a widget: the p margins inside an item box no longer collapse through it, so spacing would grow slightly. Lexical posts never have that structure. 8. Lists INSIDE other containers (quotes, collapsibles, table cells) are not covered by the selector; they follow their container's rule. 9. A bottom-aligned left widget beside a list leaves the area above the widget empty (items avoid its whole margin box). This is coherent but different from paragraphs, where text runs through that space.

design:code.baseline:
Today (Exp 2 code, no candidate CSS), rendered at 15 widths in both views (/Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/code/baseline).
- Lexical code block (reader pre.code-block, editor code.code-block). It has overflow-x:auto, so it already forms its own box. Beside a widget it narrows to whatever room is left and scrolls sideways. At a 682 column that is 425px beside a 33% widget (lines cut at about 50 characters) and 309px beside a 50% widget. A code block taller than the widget keeps that narrow width for its whole height, which leaves an empty band beside it below the widget.
- Two widgets on opposite sides, level with each other: the code box gets squeezed to the 168px between them, and even a 3-line snippet is clipped ('return p / (1'). Nothing stops this, because there is no width floor.
- Legacy pre in the reader (pre>code from CKEditor or markdown) is NOT its own box. Its grey background and 1px border run the full column width under the widget (the harness reports box overlaps PRE/CODE at every width where the widget wraps), the left border is hidden, and its pre-wrap text wraps around the float with ragged indents. This breaks the "nothing behind a widget" rule.
- Reader horizontal-scroll wrapper (MaybeScrollableBlock/HorizScrollBlock, added around root blocks wider than the column): the scroller narrows beside the widget, but the wrapper spans the full column. Its absolutely positioned arrow therefore sits at the column edge, painted over a right widget (box overlap on HorizScrollBlock-scrollIndicator at 560 to 1440). A left arrow would sit over a left widget.
- Bottom-aligned widget plus code that fits beside: works (the widget is pushed until its bottom meets the code's bottom).
- Inline code: fine. It wraps and breaks like text.
Harness note: the 'text' overlaps it reports inside code blocks are code lines clipped by the block's own scroll box, so they are false positives (the metrics ignore overflow clipping).

behaviors.block: Code block (Lexical CodeNode: editor code.code-block, reader pre.code-block)
behaviors.choice: box beside if every line fits, else below at full width
behaviors.nextToWidget: The rule is the same for left and right widgets (mirror images) and at every window width where the widget wraps. If the code's longest line plus its gutter and padding fits in the room beside the widget, the grey box sits beside the widget and fills the space from the widget's 32px gutter to the far column edge. Otherwise it starts below the widget at full column width. Room beside a widget at a 682px column (windows of 816px and up): 25%: 480px, 33%: 425px, 38%: 391px, 50%: 309px. The room shrinks with the column (window minus 128 from 600 to 815, window minus 26 below 600). Widths where nothing interacts because the widget does not wrap and shows full width: 33% below a 623px window (except 521 to 599), 38% below 663 (except 561 to 599), 25% below 726, 50% below 792, and every widget on phones. Then the code just follows the widget. When the code is the first block after the widget and does not fit, the space beside the widget stays empty, as before a heading. With a paragraph first, the paragraph wraps beside the widget and the code starts below the widget, so the gap is only what the paragraph does not fill. A code block that fits but is taller than the widget keeps its narrower width to its end, with empty space beside it below the widget. Nothing is hidden, because its lines fit. With widgets on both sides level with each other, the room is small (168px for 33% plus 33% at 682), so nearly every code block goes below both. Bottom-aligned widget: if the code fits beside, the widget is pushed down so its bottom lines up with the code's bottom, and the code sits beside it from the top (works today). If the code does not fit, the widget stays at the top with no push and the code starts below it (this needs the bottomAlign fix). Browsers without calc-size() (Safari and Firefox today) use the fallback: the box goes beside if 300px fits and scrolls there, otherwise below.
behaviors.widgetInside: n/a (a code block holds only code text)
behaviors.editor: Same as the reader: the editor's code.code-block follows the same rule (verified at every width). It has no editing chrome of its own. While the author types, the block moves below the widget as soon as a line gets too long to fit beside it, and moves back up when the line gets short enough again. A widget in code view (its source shown as a .code-block without iframe-widget-preview-mode) matches the same selector, so it follows the same rule (not screenshot-tested).
behaviors.reader: Same placement. The hover copy menu (top right of the pre) and the line-number gutter stay inside the box, so they never touch the widget. The reader's 1px border and radius are an existing editor/reader difference, unrelated to widgets.
behaviors.drag: Drop targets: when a code block needs more room than there is beside the dragged widget (its natural width is greater than column minus widget minus 32px), it counts like a clearing block (as headings and full-width widgets do). The widget is not offered bottom alignment against it, it snaps below the code block instead of landing just above it, and the code block ends the widget's section for the push-down preview. Chip: 'below the code block (too wide to sit beside the widget)'. Code that fits is an ordinary drop target, and bottom alignment against it works.

design:code.rationale: Code is the one kind of text that does not wrap, so the room beside a widget can only be spent in two ways: hide part of every line behind a sideways scroll, or put the code where it fits. Candidates A and B fill the space but truncate long code. At a 640px window, 33% (B) leaves 310px, which cuts lines at about 35 characters, and a tall block stays narrow below the widget. C is the bluntest rule, but even a 3-line snippet leaves the whole side empty. D applies the same principle as the 300px text rule (sit beside a widget only if you fit there), with "fit" meaning "every line fits" for code. Short snippets stay beside, long code gets the full column, and a widget never makes code scroll or hides any of it. The box always either fills the room beside the widget or the whole column, so it never runs under the widget and never leaves a ragged gap inside itself. Legacy pre gets the same rule, so every grey code box behaves alike. The scroll wrapper keeps the B-style "it is the box" rule. That does not prejudge the tables and math groups, and it keeps the editor and reader alike. Inline code has no real interaction, so it gets none. The cost of D is a gap beside a widget when long code follows it directly, which is the same cost headings already have. The author sees it in the editor and can put text first. Its other costs are one JS fix in bottomAlign that any "goes below" rule needs anyway, and a fit check in the drag geometry.

design:code.openIssues:
1. Editor and Post tab columns did NOT match in this run, contrary to BRIEFING.md: the editor column measured 732 against the post's 682 (editor = post + 50 at every width). As a result the editor floats widgets at 600-622 and 480-520 windows where the Post tab shows them full width, and at 480 and 640 editor content runs to the window edge. This affects every group; it needs the orchestrator.
2. calc-size() works only in Chromium (Chrome and Edge 129+). Safari and Firefox get the 300px fallback (box beside, scrolling). Use the JS --lw-code-width variant if identical behavior everywhere matters.
3. Live editing: a code block jumps below the widget the moment a typed line stops fitting beside it, and jumps back when the line gets short enough. This is honest, but it is worth Ronny's eye.
4. Long code directly after a widget leaves empty space beside the widget, the same cost as headings.
5. Cross-group: MaybeScrollableBlock replaces an overflowing root table, figure, p or math as the widget's sibling, so other groups' '~ table' / '~ figure' / '~ div' rules will not match a wrapped block; they must also target the wrapper. For consistency with this group's principle, wide tables and long equations could use the same "beside only if it fits" rule.
6. The bottomAlign runaway is generic (any block that clears or does not fit after a bottom-aligned widget). The fix in item 3 of codeChangesNeeded should land regardless of this group.
7. The .iframe-widget root div is itself eligible for MaybeScrollableBlock (rootTagShouldBeHorizontallyScrollable, ContentItemBody.tsx:38-48, accepts any div). If it were ever wrapped, the float would be trapped in the scroller and every '~' rule would break. I suggest excluding .iframe-widget there. I did not observe this happening.
8. Nested code blocks (inside collapsibles or LLM blocks) are deliberately not targeted: they follow their container's rule. Widget code view matches the selector but is not screenshot-tested, because the harness cannot toggle it.
9. The legacy pre>code import nesting in the editor (a code block inside a code block) is a separate, pre-existing bug.

design:llm-block.baseline:
Today the AI block flows beside a widget like a paragraph (it is not its own formatting context and has no border or background), and its model label is a second left float. I rendered it at all 15 widths in both views and found four problems. (1) Bottom-aligned LEFT widget: a float is placed beside the widget's whole margin box, including the push (shape-outside only moves text lines). So the floated label sits out at the widget's right edge with an empty gap before it, while the text below it starts at the column edge. Seen in both views at every wrapping width. (2) Block that does not start with a paragraph (list, heading...) after a LEFT widget: the label is a block with width:fit-content. Its text cannot fit beside the widget, so it drops below it. Its box (225px tall in the editor metrics) and its 1px right rule run straight down through the widget, leaving a hole beside the widget. Both views; the harness flags it as a box overlap in the editor at 1440 to 560. (3) Reader hit-testing: the block's position:relative plus opacity:.94 put it in a paint layer above the floated iframe, and its box spans the column under the widget. elementFromPoint at the widget's centre returns the AI block's

: 21 to 33 blocked sample points per wrapping width, for left AND right widgets. So an interactive widget beside AI text cannot be clicked in the post. The editor is fine, because its overlay has z-index 1. (4) Widget inside an AI block: in the editor it floats and hangs out of the block, so the author's next paragraph wraps beside the AI's widget. In the reader it does not show at all, because ContentItemBody drops the nested placeholder. Otherwise fine: top-aligned left and right widgets, 33% and 50%, short and long blocks, and the paragraph-before case all look good. There is no horizontal scroll at any width.

design:collapsible-spoiler.rationale:
I chose B because it is the simplest rule that fixes every real problem and looks right at every width in both views. It is one CSS declaration pair (flow-root plus a 300px floor), scoped to blocks after a floated widget, so posts without widgets are unchanged.
It removes the worst baseline bug: in the post, a hidden spoiler paints a black bar over the widget.
It makes the post match the editor, which already showed spoilers as a box beside the widget.
It keeps the collapsible's triangle, rule and indent together beside the widget instead of under it.
It treats every bordered or backgrounded box in this group the same way, and the same way the code group's candidate B does.
Collapsible sections are published closed, and closed sections beside a widget then look like ordinary lines. Opening one grows the box in place, with no jump.
It leaves the author free to put any of these blocks beside a widget. The one cost, long open content staying narrow below the widget, is visible in the editor, so the author can move the widget if they dislike it.
Bottom alignment and drag work without JS.
Clearing below (C) wastes the space beside the widget, especially for closed sections. It also breaks bottom alignment unless JS changes. Flowing beside with fixed decorations is not possible: a block that is not its own box cannot keep a left rule clear of a transparent float.

A left widget gets the collapsible's triangle drawn on it, the grey rule shows through it, and the indent jumps. The legacy block's border runs through the widget. Editor and post disagree for spoilers.

rejected.name: C. Clears below
rejected.why: Leaves large empty areas beside the widget, especially for closed sections (three titles all pushed under a 50% widget). Never lets a section or spoiler sit beside a widget. A bottom-aligned widget before a clearing block runs away hundreds of px down (bottomAlign.ts keeps pushing because the block moves with it), so it would need JS.

rejected.why: The triangle could follow the text. But the content's left rule (border-left) cannot follow the widget edge unless the content is its own box. The widget is transparent, so the rule would still show through it, and the 25px indent would still be lost beside a left widget.

rejected.why: Needs JS measuring. Still leaves gaps for long blocks. The decision would flip when a reader opens a closed section, so the section would jump below the widget mid-read.

design:tables.rationale: The same rule as every other bordered or backgrounded box: a table sits beside a widget when it fits, otherwise below. It makes the editor and post identical (today they disagree for every table), lets an author pair a short table with a widget, keeps wide tables at full width instead of scrolling them beside a widget, and makes bottom alignment with a table work. The width condition needs no extra threshold: a wrapping widget always leaves 300px, so only the table's own narrowest layout decides. Pure CSS left one visible glitch (a table sitting beside only the widget's last few pixels stays narrow for its whole height), so a small sliver guard sends such a table below. Candidate A (always clear) looked clean for long tables but left a hole beside the widget whenever a table followed it, could never pair a table with a widget, and broke bottom alignment; Ronny's pattern is the simpler rule that leaves the author more freedom.

(2) Make the widget-inside-a-list-item case actually contained. I would also make the rule apply after left widgets only, because D brings no benefit beside right widgets and only costs space there. judge:lists:author.notes:
Lens: author and robustness. I re-rendered my own specimen (/Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/design/lists/judge-author/gen.mjs, spec.html) with baseline and final CSS at 1440, 800, 700, 640, 599 and 560, in both views. Output is in /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/lists/judge-author/{base,final,final-recheck,final-early}. Sections tested: widget inside an item with no earlier widget, R33/L50/R50 bottom-aligned with long lists, left and right widgets level, two stacked left widgets with a list between, ol start=98, and lists far below a widget.

Confirmed good:
- Scoping holds. Lists far below a wrapping widget (3-level nested ol, checklist, ol start=7) are pixel-identical to baseline in the editor at all 6 widths. In the post, the only differences are iframe paint inside the widget box.
- Two widgets level (L25 + R25): D keeps the straddling item in the middle column, which is cleaner than baseline's jump.
- Stacked left widgets: fine, and editor and post agree.
- Long URLs and long inline code never push an item box below the widget. word-break: break-word applies in both views, so min-content stays small (judge-reader J-L33-url shots).
- 0 overlaps and no sideways scroll anywhere.
- With CSS present from load, the editor's bottom-align loop converges with D and matches the post.

D's top-aligned left behavior is the real win: nested levels stay nested, and typing past the widget's bottom no longer makes lines jump left. It is the finest-grained box approach possible, so it leaves less empty space than B. Its weak spots are all bottom alignment (a box ignores shape-outside and avoids the whole margin box) plus paragraph-long bullets beside right widgets. Hence my recommendations: no bottom-align next to lists, and preferably apply the rule after left widgets only. That needs a side flag (data-lw-wraps=left|right; a lwFloatedLeft class in the reader). Even then, `~` cannot pick the NEAREST widget, so alternating-side posts are only partly covered. `.L ~ ul:not(.L ~ .R ~ ul)` covers left-then-right but wrongly excludes left, right, left, list.

Also worth fixing outside the lists CSS: a widget inside a list item vanishes in the Post tab (empty placeholder). The display fallback in JSS should use `fallbacks`, as the designer said.

judge:columns:author.notes:
I agree with D. It is the most predictable rule for an author. The columns look the same with or without a widget and at every width, they match headings and full-width widgets, and the editor and Post tab agree. I checked the designer's final2 metrics: the nested sections are 0 to 1px apart and the rest match the baseline's own offsets. My adversarial run (11 extra sections, 12 widths, both views, specimen at /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/design/columns/judge-author/spec.html) found no overlaps, no sideways scroll and no CSS leaking onto posts without widgets. C's short-columns-beside-a-33%-widget case does look nicer at desktop width, but it flips between beside and below with the window width, and it needs extra JS. B destroys the column layout. D's cost is a blank area beside a widget that columns directly follow, the same as headings. The drag snap-below plan handles that only for drags, not for typed or inserted columns.

Caveats for Ronny. (1) Columns cannot be created today. Choosing D means turning on a new block type: an importDOM fix, theme classes, sanitize allowlist entries and an insert entry. That is a product decision, and it should be made explicitly, not as a side effect. (2) The stand-ins in final.css (the !important bottom-align override and the forced full-width nested widget) should not ship as CSS. (3) Optional author aid: an editor-only faint outline on columns. Stacked columns look like plain paragraphs, so otherwise the author cannot tell they are inside a column. (4) Optional refinement: when 3 columns have stacked, they could stop clearing, which would avoid the unexplained blank. That is hard to do with container queries, because a query cannot change the container itself, so I would not block on it.

Scratch files are in /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/design/columns/judge-author/ and screenshots in /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/judge-author/.

design:columns.baseline: Columns do not exist for authors today, so there is nothing to interact with. There is no way to insert them: the "Columns Layout" toolbar item is commented out (lexical/plugins/ToolbarPlugin/index.tsx:1309-1321), ToolbarPlugin is not mounted, and the slash menu has no entry. Even pasted or saved columns HTML does not survive. LayoutContainerNode.importDOM reads grid-template-columns through window.getComputedStyle (LayoutContainerNode.ts:31-43), and that returns nothing for the DOMParser documents the editor imports from (Editor.tsx:821-825). The container is dropped and LayoutPlugin unwraps the orphaned items (LayoutPlugin.tsx:104-115, 215-235), so the editor shows plain paragraphs (verified by probe: 5 paragraph nodes, no layout nodes). Nothing gives the block display:grid either: theme.layoutContainer and layoutItem are commented out (PlaygroundEditorTheme.ts:68-69) and no CSS mentions it. The real reader gets bare nested divs, because sanitize.ts strips div style and the data-lexical-layout-* attributes (div attributes at :177, div classes at :276-312). The Post tab renders unsanitized HTML, so it keeps the attributes, but still has no grid. The result in both views: the "columns" are stacked paragraphs that flow beside a widget like any text. Rendered at all 15 widths: no overlaps and no sideways scroll. Two other problems turned up. (1) Widgets nested in ANY block never render in the reader or Post tab. ContentItemBody.tsx:495-500 returns a childless non-root element as `<TagName {...attribs}/>` and drops its hydrated `result`, so the empty `.iframe-widget` placeholder inside a column, quote, list or collapsible stays empty (seen here and in the quote group's shots). (2) The editor sizes a nested widget against the root column, not its container (IframeWidgetPlugin.tsx:565, widgetDragDom.ts:23-28). A 33% widget inside a ~330px column therefore floats at 225px in the editor, with text squeezed beside it, while the reader (container-measured) would show it full width. Baseline section heights for the nested sections differ by 78 to 225px between editor and post.

design:columns.rationale: Columns need width, and an author who chose two or three columns chose a layout that should not change because a widget is nearby. Clearing below keeps the columns identical at every window width with or without a widget, and it is a single, predictable rule. It is also the rule LessWrong already uses for other structural blocks that need the whole column: headings, full-width widgets and the footnote section all start below a float. The two box-beside variants (B and C) give the author slightly more freedom, but the freedom produces bad results. A grid that sits beside a float keeps its narrowed width for its whole height, so long columns leave a blank area under the widget. And since columns must stack when too narrow, a widget next to them either destroys the column layout (B) or makes it jump between beside and below as the window or widget width changes (C), which the author cannot predict from the editor. Inside a column, full width is the honest answer: the existing wrap rule (300px of text beside, 150px minimum widget) can never be met in a column at LessWrong's widths, so "full width there" is what the rule already says, and the editor just has to agree with the reader. One caveat: columns cannot be created at all today. If Ronny does not want to turn them on, the behavior is "no interaction" (they are plain paragraphs), and only the general nested-widget reader bug matters.

rejected.name: No change (baseline)
rejected.why: There are no columns: the block cannot be inserted, and saved columns import as paragraphs (editor) and bare divs (reader). It is fine only if columns stay off. It is the right answer in that case and is noted in openIssues.

rejected.name: B: box beside, stacking when narrow
rejected.why: Long columns stay narrow for their whole height with a blank area under the widget, and beside a 50% widget (or at mid widths) the columns stack into a narrow strip of paragraphs, so the author's 2 or 3 columns disappear even on desktop (e.g. /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/cands/B/post-599-l33-2col-long.png, /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/cands/B/post-1440-r50-3col-short.png).

rejected.why: Short columns beside a 25% or 33% widget at desktop look good, but long columns leave the same blank under the widget. Beside versus below flips with window width and widget width (unpredictable to the author), and it needs extra JS (bottom alignment runs away wherever the columns drop below the widget). Too much rule for one nice case.

design:columns.openIssues:
1. Columns are not an author feature today: there is no insert UI, the import drops them, and the sanitizer strips them. Whether to turn them on is Ronny's call. If they stay off, the honest behavior is "no interaction" (they are paragraphs), and only the reader bug in 3 matters.
2. Stacked 3 columns (column under 600px, windows 600-727 and 521-599 with a wrapping 33% or 38% widget) still clear below the widget although they then look like paragraphs, leaving a blank beside the widget. Letting stacked columns flow beside the widget would need the post column itself as a size container (container-type on the post body and editor root), so the block can switch to display:block when narrow. Left out for simplicity. 2 columns never hit this, since they stack only under 400px, where no widget wraps.
3. Reader bug outside this group (affects quotes, lists, collapsibles, footnotes, LLM blocks): ContentItemBody.tsx:495-500 never renders a widget nested in any block. My Post tab shots of nested widgets are a simulation of the fix.
4. The bottom-alignment runaway (bottomAlign.ts) is general: any next block that clears (headings too) or drops below the widget makes the push grow without bound. The prototype pins such widgets to the top with CSS. The real fix is in alignedParagraph/alignFloatBottom, plus the gear hiding Bottom there.
5. Pre-existing editor/post offsets the columns rules do not change (same in the baseline): +6 to +8px where a widget is full width, and +18px for a bottom-aligned widget at 560-700 windows.
6. The stacking thresholds (about 190px per column, so 2 columns need 400px and 3 need 600px) are my choice; uneven templates (1:3) get a narrower small column (about 164px at 682). 4 columns would always be stacked at the normal width, so do not offer them.
7. The editor's mismatch (it sizes nested widgets against the root column) is shared with every container. Other groups may pick "same wrap rule measured against the container", which gives the same result here (full width in every realistic column).

My lens was author and robustness. I re-rendered the designer's spec with a harness copy that puts the CSS in the page from load and scrolls so lazy iframes can load (/Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/design/quote/judge-author/render-early.mjs). What holds up:
- Editor and Post agree, including bottom alignment, once the CSS is present from the start. The 1440 mismatch in the designer's screenshots is a harness artifact. In the real code, placeSpacer sets data-lw-wraps before alignFloatBottom measures, and alignment re-runs on every edit.
- CSS scoping is clean. A quote far below the widgets (with a list and a nested quote) is visually identical to baseline in both views; the pixel diff is only sub-pixel anti-aliasing. Posts without a wrapping widget never match the selectors.
- Two widgets: stacked same-side widgets of different widths (25% over 50%, 50% over 25%) and staggered left/right widgets give no overlaps. Chrome narrows the quote enough to clear the wider float over its whole height, or moves it below the left widget when less than 300px fits.

Known costs, real but acceptable and visible to the author:
- A long quote stays narrow under the widget. Stacked 25%+50% widgets leave about 270px of quote text with about 340px of blank beside it at 1440.
- min-width 300 counts the border box, so quote text can be as narrow as 265px at the narrowest wrapping widths (33% at windows 521 to 555). Raising it to min(335px,100%) would honor the 300px-of-text rule, but it pushes those quotes below the widget at those widths. It is optional; I would not force it.

Outside this group: a post holding a wide table or long display math widens the editor column to 732px while the post stays at 682, in A and B alike. That is pre-existing and belongs to the tables and math groups. I did not test the near-miss case (a quote whose top barely touches the widget's bottom margin, then stays narrow); the reader judge is rendering it.

problems: Unequal templates get too narrow before they stack. The stacking threshold counts columns (2 stack under 400px, 3 under 600px) and ignores the fr ratio. In a 1:3 layout at windows 426 to 520 (column 400 to 494) the narrow column is 94 to 117px, so it holds about one or two words per line: /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/final2/post-480-in-1-3.png. The proposed sanitize rule (^(\d+fr ?){2,3}$) and importDOM accept any ratio, so these layouts will reach readers.

The 'widget inside a column' reasoning is wrong for stacked 3-column blocks. It says no realistic layout can wrap inside a column. But once 3 columns stack (windows 521 to 599 and 600 to 727), each item is the full column, 472 to 599px wide. By the reader's container-measured rule a 33% widget wraps there from 495px (windows 521 to 599 and 623 to 727), and a 38% widget wraps from 535px (windows 561 to 599 and 663 to 727). final.css section 4 forces full width in both views, which hides this: /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/final2/post-700-in-3col.png. If the editor never wraps and the reader is not forced, the editor will show the widget full width while the post floats it, at those widths.

At windows 521 to 599 and 623 to 727, a 3-column block after a wrapping widget looks like ordinary paragraphs, yet it leaves a blank of about 330x170px beside the widget, where normal paragraphs would flow: /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/judge-reader/variants/post-727-l33-short-3col.png (compare /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/judge-reader/variants/post-728-l33-short-3col.png). The wide column of a 1:3 layout at the 682px column is 493.5px, and the nested widget's right edge is clipped: /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/final2/post-1440-in-1-3.png, /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/judge-reader/crop-post-1440-in-1-3-right.png. The general fix is to round widget widths to whole pixels.

Side issue not caused by columns: in the Post tab, a bottom-aligned widget next to a paragraph taller than itself is not pushed down at all, while the editor aligns it. This happens even in a control with no columns and no candidate CSS: /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/judge-reader/bottom/none/post-1440-ctrl-bottom-longpara-para.png vs /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/columns/judge-reader/variants/editor-1440-r33-bottom-longpara-2col.png. The DOM probe meant to confirm it was still queued for a browser slot when I had to report.
mustFix: Stack by the narrowest column, not by the number of columns. Either limit templates to a fixed set with their own thresholds (1:1 stacks under 400px, 1:1:1 under 600px, 1:2 or 2:1 under about 560px so the narrow column stays at least about 180px), using template classes instead of a free fr regex in sanitize.ts and importDOM. Or allow only equal columns. Today a 1:3 block at windows 426 to 520 has a 94 to 117px column (final2/post-480-in-1-3.png).

Make 'a widget inside a column always shows at the column's full width' a required rule in BOTH views. In the reader, force floated=false when iframe.closest('.layout-column'), not 'optionally'. In the editor, do not wrap inside a layout item. Also correct the rationale: once 3 columns stack, each item is the full column (472 to 599px), and the measured rule would wrap a 33% widget at windows 521 to 599 and 623 to 727 (38% from 561 and from 663), so leaving the reader unforced makes editor and post disagree.

revise:footnotes.rationale: Footnotes are end matter, so they should start under a widget, not wrap around it. "Clears below" is the simplest rule, matches how headings already behave, and the Exp 2 editor already does it, so the reader just catches up. It gave zero overlaps at all 15 widths in both views, and both judges found the same from 2560 to 320 with their own edge cases (opposite-side pairs, stacked widgets, tall 50% widgets, 25% Bottom widgets, widget-first footnotes, posts with no widget or an early widget). It only acts while a widget really floats, so it needs no width-specific cases and does nothing to posts without widgets. The author keeps full freedom: the widget stays where it was put. The v1 write-up wrongly offered Bottom alignment as a way to fill the space beside a widget whose following text is shorter; the judges were right (bottomAlign only pushes down, push 0 there), so the text now says the author moves the widget up or adds text. The judges were also right about shipping order: the reader clear rule turns the existing bottom-align runaway into a post-page bug (about 620px of blank page at 1440), so the clear rules and the bottomAlign fix ship as one change. The proposed fix is a single geometric test (a block that starts at or below the widget's bottom is not beside it, so no push). On the real page it returns 0 before the footnotes and before an h2, and leaves correct pushes unchanged (82-134px with a long paragraph, 0 with a short one) at 1440, 800 and 599 in the reader and at 1440 in the editor. It also fixes the same runaway that headings already cause today. For a widget inside a footnote, full width is the simplest rule and looks fine at every width. Previews show a stand-in rather than the widget: the sidenote is too small and fades out, and a live copy in each preview would drift out of step with the real one. A link to the footnote keeps the widget in one place. The 16px rule gap under a widget is kept: it is the widget's normal bottom margin, matches headings, and a CSS-only fix would only cover the case with nothing between the widget and the footnotes. Markers and sidenotes need no float rule, so none is forced.

rejected.name: No change

rejected.name: B: box beside (flow-root + min-width 300px)

rejected.name: C: flows beside (rule redrawn as a narrow flow-root strip, footnote text made inline)
rejected.why: Rewrites footnote internals. Loses the hanging indent. The rule is indented by the list padding. Editor and reader break lines differently. Fragile for little benefit.

rejected.name: Widget inside a footnote floats inside it
rejected.why: Needs the editor to size and wrap against the footnote's own width (it uses the root column today), shrinks the text beside it below the 300px rule at mid widths, and duplicates float logic for a rare case. Full width is simpler and looks fine.

rejected.name: Previews run the nested widget (v1 plan: fix 7 alone)
rejected.why: The sidenote is capped at 200px with a 40px gradient fade, so the widget shows cut off under a gradient (previews-v1/post-1440-sidenote.png), which breaks the no-gradient-on-widgets rule. rejected.name: Previews run the widget in an uncapped sidenote
rejected.why: A 226px-wide margin widget is cramped, a tall sidenote pushes the following sidenotes down, and it still runs a second live copy. The stand-in link is simpler.

rejected.name: Bottom alignment as the fix for empty space beside a last widget (v1 text)
rejected.why: Wrong: alignFloatBottom only pushes a widget down to end with a paragraph taller than it; with a shorter paragraph the push is 0 (judge shots judge-author/final/post-1440-j-bottom-shortpara.png, and t-short push 0 in both views in v2-bottom). rejected.name: Prefilter only on computed clear (judge option a)

rejected.name: Even out the 16px gap above the rule with CSS
rejected.why: Clearing swallows the section's 40px top margin. CSS can only enlarge the widget's bottom margin when the footnotes come directly after it, which leaves the paragraph-in-between case at 16px and changes text wrapping below that widget. Headings that clear sit 16px under a widget too, so the current spacing is consistent across Experiment 3.

I re-rendered final.css with an edge-case specimen (~/lw-exp3-proto/design/footnotes/judge-author/judge-spec.html) at 1440, 1100, 816, 760, 700, 640, 599, 560 and 540. Results:

(3) Drag-lens remark only: snapping a widget aimed just above a divider to below it moves the widget into the next section. design:embeds.baseline:
Experiment 2 code today. Every embed wrapper is a plain block (no formatting context, no margins), so its box starts beside a floated widget and runs under it. What goes wrong depends on the embed.

- **YouTube (post):** div.youtube-preview is a full-column 16:9 padding box. Its absolutely positioned iframe paints OVER the widget. When it comes right after the widget it covers the widget completely; after a short paragraph it covers the widget's lower half. In the editor the same video is a fixed 560x315 inline iframe that drops below the widget, so the editor and the post disagree. That fixed 560px iframe also made the editor column wider than the post column at windows of 640px and below (editor 560 vs post 534 at 560; 504 vs 454 at 480).
- **Metaculus:** its dark #2c3947 background fills the band beside and under the widget, in both views. The clear widget then sits on a dark slab, and its dark-green content almost disappears.
- **Manifold, Metaforecast, OWID, LW Artifacts, Thoughtsaver, Neuronpedia, Calendly:** the 100%-wide inline iframe cannot fit beside the float, so it already drops below it. Only the invisible top of the wrapper sits beside the widget.

- **StrawPoll, logged-out readers:** they get a bordered "This poll is hidden" box. Its border runs under the widget and its absolutely positioned 4px yellow bar paints across the widget.
- **Elicit claim:** the flex histogram row narrows beside the widget, but the 1%...99% title row drops below it, so the block comes apart.

Harness metrics:
- Post: 8 box overlaps at windows 800-1440 (YouTube x3, Metaculus background x2, StrawPoll box/bar x3) and 6 at 560-700. None where widgets do not wrap.
- Editor: 2 overlaps (Metaculus background).
- No horizontal scroll anywhere.

Bug found: an align=bottom widget whose next block is an embed is pushed down by about one embed height (403px in the post at 1440). The embed always ends below the widget, so the bottom-align loop keeps pushing. Once embeds clear, this push grows without bound across resizes (2,528px in the post at 1440, 253,278px in the editor at 560).

design:embeds.rationale:
Embeds are fixed-size frames made for the full column. Most of them are fixed height (300-750px), and YouTube's height follows its width. Placed beside a widget (candidate C) they keep the narrow width for their whole height. Metaculus turns into a 309x400 phone layout and Calendly into a 380x750 strip, with a large empty area under the widget. Videos shrink to half size. Today's behavior (A) puts YouTube on top of the widget, puts Metaculus's dark background under it, and runs the StrawPoll login bar across it.

"Starts below the widget" is one simple rule that is correct at every width, left and right, top and bottom aligned:
- The embed always gets its full size.
- Nothing ever runs under or over a widget (0 overlaps, no horizontal scroll at 15 widths in both views).
- The editor and the post match.

It is also the rule Experiment 2 already uses for the nearest relative of an embed, a full-width widget, which clears floats. So "frames never sit beside frames" holds across widgets and embeds. Because the editor's drag code reads computed clear, embeds plug into the existing snap-below and pushes-down logic.

The cost is the same as for headings: an embed placed right after a widget leaves empty space beside the widget, and the drag code steers authors away from that. The hybrid (D) would keep videos beside widgets, but only by shrinking them and adding a second rule. The CTA button and the unreachable nodes get no rule because they can never meet a widget.

design:embeds.editorDom:
**Editor** (Lexical root `[data-lexical-editor]`):
- A wrapping widget is the spacer `code.iframe-widget-code.iframe-widget-preview-mode[data-lw-wraps]`, floated by placeSpacer. Each widget is followed by a zero-height `p.sentinel-paragraph`.
- Each embed is a top-level `div[data-lexical-decorator="true"][contenteditable=false]` (LexicalDecoratorBlockNode.createDOM, no class). Inside it is `div[style="text-align:…"]` (BlockWithAlignableContents, no class), then the embed:
  - `div.metaculus-preview[data-metaculus-id]`, `div.manifold-preview`, `div.metaforecast-preview`, `div.owid-preview`, `div.neuronpedia-preview`, `div.calendly-preview`, `div.lwartifacts-preview` (iframe inline style height 500), `div.thoughtSaverFrameWrapper > iframe.thoughtSaverFrame`, `div.estimaker-preview` / `div.viewpoints-preview` (display:flex), each holding an iframe.
  - `div.strawpoll-embed#strawpoll_ID`, inline style height 480, max-width 640, flex column.
  - YouTube: a bare `iframe[width=560][height=315][src*=youtube-nocookie]` directly inside the alignable div.
- Elicit: top-level `div.elicit-binary-prediction-wrapper[data-lexical-decorator]` > `div.elicit-binary-prediction-editor-preview` (margin 8px 0) > ElicitBlock.
- Selector: `.iframe-widget-code[data-lw-wraps] ~ :is([data-lexical-decorator]:has(> div > :is(iframe, .metaculus-preview, …)), .elicit-binary-prediction-wrapper)`. A `~ * …` variant catches embeds inside containers.

**Reader** (post body):
- The widget is `div.iframe-widget > iframe.lwFloatedWidget`.
- Each embed is a top-level sibling: `div.youtube-preview > iframe` (absolute), `div.metaculus-preview`, … `div.thoughtSaverFrameWrapper`. Rendered through MaybeScrollableBlock, which adds no wrapper unless the content overflows.
- `div.strawpoll-embed`: children replaced by WrappedStrawPoll. Logged out, that is `div.WrappedStrawPoll-loginRequired` (border, position relative) with `div.WrappedStrawPoll-yellowBar` (absolute).
- `div.elicit-binary-prediction`: children replaced by ElicitBlock (ContentStyles root, flex histogram row, flex title row).
- Selector: `.iframe-widget:has(> .lwFloatedWidget) ~ :is(div.youtube-preview, …, div.elicit-binary-prediction)`, plus a `~ * …` variant.

design:embeds.openIssues:
1. **Bottom-align JS fix is required** before shipping B. The final CSS only stands in for it (a `!important` margin-top on floats whose next block is an embed). Without it, align=bottom widgets before an embed run away downward.
2. **Drag geometry changes are described, not prototyped:** measureBlocks marking embeds as clearing, and the 'Below the embed' / 'pushes the embed down' chip text.
3. **The YouTube editor-parity rule in final.css applies to every post in the editor** (not scoped to widgets), on purpose: it makes the editor match the post, and the real fix is in YouTubeComponent. It also removed the editor-column mismatch at windows of 640px and below. The code group's runs show the same mismatch (editor 584 vs post 534 at 560), probably from fixed-width content as well.
4. **Pre-existing editor vs post size differences, untouched:** StrawPoll (editor 480px flex box, max 640px, centered; post 400px full-width iframe), LW Artifacts (500 vs 525px), Calendly src parameters.
5. **Bottom-aligned sections sit about 18px lower in the editor than in the post** (constant offset, same relative layout). This is about bottom alignment or sentinel paragraphs, not embeds.
6. **Harness caveat for other agents:** proto-render.mjs's fullPage section shots do not paint cross-origin iframes (widgets, embeds) that were never on screen, so lower sections show widgets as missing. I used a copy, /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/design/embeds/render.mjs (tall viewport, scrolls each section into view, falls back to fullPage). The shared harness is unchanged.
7. **Embeds inside containers:** the `~ *` selectors make an embed inside a container that flows beside a widget start below the widget inside that container (tested with a quote). The container's own box behavior belongs to the containers groups.
8. **Unverified:** the logged-in StrawPoll iframe in the Post tab (headless is logged out) and Elicit with real data (the local DB returned no question).

judge:widgets-text-inline:reader.notes:
Verdict: I agree with the chosen Final (B plus the scroll-arrow wrapper) over A and C, with the three fixes above.

Why it is right for readers:
- At level, opposite widgets left 100-280px strips of text (worse: 18px for 50%+38%).
- C's centered widget sitting off-center beside a float looks accidental.
- Stacking makes opposite floats follow the same rule as same-side floats.

What I checked:
- Rendered the designer's spec2 shots, plus my own specimens at 1440, 1100, 900, 816, 800, 760, 700, 640, 610, 599, 560, 480 and 360 in both views, with final.css and proto.js.
- Specimens covered: tall right widget then left, long text under stacked pairs, 25+25, 50+33, 50+38, 38+38, a bottom-aligned widget after an opposite one with a long paragraph, same-side pair then opposite, a centered 25% alone, centered after R50, a widget followed by a quote or a list, a heading or list before a widget, and a full-width widget before a floated one.
- No horizontal scroll and no widget overlap from this group's CSS at any width. The only overlap flagged is the blockquote border, which belongs to the quote group.
- No CSS leaks onto posts without widgets. Every rule is scoped to .lwFloatedWidget or data-lw-wraps. The HorizScrollBlock flow-root rule changes nothing visible when no widget is beside it: the post-width spec-huge no-widget shots are pixel identical at 1100 and 800. This is because the scroller's -1em margins cancel out either way.
- The scroll-arrow fix works: the arrow is now beside the R50 widget, not on it.
- Inline content needs no rule. Long URLs, words and code break or move below the widget with no overlap.
- With text blocks before widgets, editor and post match to the pixel at every width where widgets wrap. The exceptions are listed under problems.

Lower-priority problems:
- A bottom-aligned widget after an opposite one cannot keep its alignment when the paragraph is short. Reword the behavior text, or have the editor warn.
- Centered-widget vertical spacing differs between the views (editor text 8-16px lower).
- A widget placed beside text can drift well below that text. This is inherent and the same as same-side stacking.

design:headings.baseline:
Today (Exp 2 code) the editor clears h1 to h3 after a wrapping widget (IframeWidgetPlugin.tsx:461-466). The reader clears only h1 and h2 (HydratedIframeWidget.tsx:70-79). h4 to h6 flow beside the widget in both views. Problems seen:

(2) Clearing leaves holes. A heading right after a widget leaves the widget alone with an empty half-column beside it (h2-direct-R50, h2-direct-L33 at 700). A short section beside a tall widget leaves a 100 to 250px blank area before the next h2 (h2-mid-L33, short-sec-L33).
(3) Runaway bottom push. A widget with align=bottom followed by a heading that clears it gets pushed far down, because the heading always moves below it and alignFloatBottom keeps pushing. The section measured 3590 to 5731px in the editor and 1476 to 3146px in the post, against about 340 to 430px without the clear.
(4) Dragging treats every HeadingNode (h1 to h6) as a section break: it snaps below it, cuts the ghost at it and says "pushes the heading down". But h4 to h6 never clear, so for them the chip is wrong.
(5) The `~` rule only matches headings with the same parent, so a widget inside a quote or collapsible never clears headings after that container.

design:headings.rationale: Clearing was Claude's default. By eye it is the worst of the four: whenever a section is shorter than the widget beside it, or a heading directly follows a widget, it leaves a blank hole beside the widget (100 to 250px at 682px, half the column at 50%). The hole size changes with window width, so the author cannot design around it. It also causes the runaway bottom-align push. Letting headings sit beside the widget removes all holes at every width, treats h1 to h6 the same (fixing the editor/reader h3 mismatch and the wrong drag chips for h4 to h6), and leaves the author free: a heading can sit beside a widget, or above it by dropping the widget below the heading. Plain flowing text (C) breaks long headings around a left widget's corner. One flow-root rule (D) fixes that and reuses the 300px rule and the 'box beside' primitive other blocks use. Print and wiki layouts (for example Wikipedia's floated images) let a figure run beside the next section's heading, so this reads as normal.

rejected.name: A: all clear
rejected.why: Holes beside the widget whenever the section is shorter than the widget or the heading follows it directly. It removes the author's option of a heading beside a widget, and without a separate fix it keeps the runaway bottom push.

rejected.name: B: major clear, minor flow (reader today)
rejected.why: Same holes for h1 and h2, the levels LessWrong authors actually use for sections. It is a rule keyed to heading level, which authors choose for size, not layout.

rejected.name: C: all flow beside as plain text
rejected.why: Almost right and simplest, but a multi-line heading that crosses a left widget's bottom edge splits into an indented first line and full-width rest (h1-mid-L50 at 1100). D fixes this with one CSS rule.

judge:code:author.notes: I agree with D. Code is the one block that cannot wrap, so 'beside only if every line fits' is the right extension of the 300px text rule. It never makes a reader miss code because of a widget, it fixes the legacy pre background running under the widget and the scroll arrow painting over a right widget, and its cost (an empty band beside the widget) is the same one headings already have. B is simpler for the author and never jumps while typing, but it truncates long code beside the widget to about 35-57 characters. That hurts readers more than the gap costs, and B stays as the graceful fallback anyway. Scoping is good: every selector needs a floated widget (data-lw-wraps / .lwFloatedWidget), legacy pre gets display:flow-root only after a floated widget, and I saw no horizontal page scroll at any width in either view. Inline code needs nothing. Recommended change: fold the 300px floor into calc-size, using clamp(min(300px, 100%), size, 100%), so short snippets do not squeeze into gaps under 300px between two widgets and Chromium agrees with the fallback for every snippet under 300px. I tested this in both views. Strongly consider the designer's step 5 (a JS-measured --lw-code-width) if Safari and Firefox must match. The scroll-wrapper rule (a box with a 300px floor) contradicts D's own principle: the wrapped content is by definition wider than the column, and a wide table squeezed beside a widget shows one column. That is acceptable only because the tables and math groups own it, and they must target the wrapper. design:widgets-text-inline.rationale:
The simplest rule that holds at every width is that a widget never sits level with a widget before it.
- For floats this is just clear: both, and it is what the 300px-of-text rule already implies. With the offered widths, two opposite floats level with each other can never leave 300px between them (25% + 25% leaves 277px at the widest column). Today's level pairs produce 100-280px strips of text at every width where both wrap.
- For centered widgets it means center really is centered: the widget gets its own row, the same as a full-width widget. It is drawn at its width in both views, so the editor finally shows what the post shows.
- Inline content needs nothing. Break-word keeps URLs, long words and inline code inside the room beside a widget. An unbreakable equation either fits beside (300px is a lot of math) or moves below, the same in both views. Forcing anything there would need per-equation JS.
- Two editor-only fixes make the editor match the post: the caret line stays out of the widget, and the text after a widget starts where the post starts it. Both were found while testing, not by assumption.
- One reader fix stops the scroll arrow from being drawn on a widget.
- Candidate C kept the reader as is, but its centered widget lands off-center beside a float and the squeezed text remains.

rejected.name: A: no change
rejected.why: Squeezed 100-280px text between opposite floats; reader and editor disagree on centered widgets (beside versus full width below); caret line across the widget; text after every widget about 1em lower in the editor; scroll arrow painted on a right widget.

rejected.name: C: beside when it fits
rejected.why: Keeps the squeezed text. A centered widget becomes an off-center neighbour of the float with text only below both, which is not what center means. More special cases for no gain.

rejected.name: JS rule: opposite floats level only if 300px of text remains
rejected.why: For every offered width it gives the same result as clear: both (25%+25% leaves 277px in the widest 682px column), so the CSS rule is the simpler form. It would differ only for pixel widths, which the editor does not offer.

rejected.name: Sentinel margin fix by a negative top margin on the sentinel after the widget
rejected.why: No effect in Chrome (probe at 1100: offsets unchanged).

rejected.name: Sentinel margin fix by hiding the sentinel's
rejected.why: Matched paragraphs, but moved the text after full-width widgets by 9px, and it risks the browser's own caret navigation into the sentinel, which needs that line box.

rejected.name: Fitting long inline math to the room beside a widget (shrink or scroll)
rejected.why: CSS cannot size an inline box to the room beside a float, because percentages resolve against the paragraph. It would need JS per equation, and moving the line below the widget is honest and identical in both views. Not forced.

1. Opposite floats stacking reverses an Exp 2 decision that Claude made without Ronny ('allowed, warned'). He should approve it, and the Exp 2 drag tests that expect data-beside-opposite need updating. 2. Centered widgets have no 150px floor. A 25% centered widget is 118-180px at 600-815px windows (128px at 640, with its label wrapping) in both views. I recommend the floats' MIN_WIDGET_WIDTH rule (full width under 150px) for center too. Not prototyped (it needs JS). 3. The editor's non-wrapping spacer keeps the .code-block margin of 8px 0, and the sentinels block margin collapsing. So full-width and centered widgets, and the text after them, sit about 8px lower in the editor than in the post. This was already true for full width. A fix is margin-block 0 on .iframe-widget-preview-mode:not([data-lw-wraps]) (for center, 0 auto). Not prototyped. 4. Not a widget interaction: an inline equation wider than the column never scrolls in the editor and overflows past the column. On the demo page it widens the whole editor column (a grid item with min-width auto): 732 vs 682 at desktop with a 750px equation, and 370 vs 334 at a 360 window with the 400px binomial, where text is clipped at the window edge. The reader scrolls it instead. This is for the math group. 5. The margin-top: 0 fix assumes the next block's top margin is at most the previous block's bottom margin (both 1em for p, ul, blockquote). A block with a larger top margin would sit slightly higher in the editor than in the post. 6. The sentinel caret was shown by adding the sentinel-focused class from a script, with the blink frozen for screenshots. Real keyboard navigation into a flow-root sentinel was not exercised. My copy, render-js.mjs, scrolls each section into view at a 2400px viewport. 8. With clear: both, sections cascade: a widget placed shortly after a tall widget on the other side starts below it.
