behaviors.choice: beside if it fits at its own size, else below
behaviors.nextToWidget: The image keeps its natural width, capped at the column. Free space beside a floated widget = column minus widget minus the 32px gutter; in the 682px column that is 479px beside a 25% widget, 425px beside 33%, 391px beside 38%, 309px beside 50%. If the image is no wider than the free space it sits beside the widget, centred in that space (to the left of a right widget, to the right of a left widget), starting where it would start anyway: level with the widget's top when it directly follows the widget, or partway down when a paragraph comes first. Text after it runs beside whatever is left of the widget, then full width. If the image is wider, it starts below the widget (after the widget's 16px bottom margin), centred in the column, and the space beside the widget above it stays blank, as today. So full-size photos and screenshots (most images, wider than about 480px) always go below at every width; small images sit beside. The free space shrinks with the window, so a small image can switch: a 320px image after a 33% widget sits beside at windows of about 654px and up and 552 to 599, and goes below (centred) at 623 to 653 and 521 to 551. Where the widget does not wrap (25% under 726px windows, 33% at 600 to 622 and under 521, 38% at 600 to 662 and under 561, 50% under 792, and all phones) the widget is full width and the image simply follows it: no interaction. Bottom-aligned widget: if the image sits beside it and is taller, the widget's bottom lines up with the image's bottom; if the image is shorter the widget stays at the top (as with a short paragraph); if the image is below the widget there is nothing beside it to line up with and the widget stays at the top (needs the bottomAlign fix; today the editor pushes widget and image down without limit). Left and right widgets behave symmetrically.
behaviors.editor: The editor now places the image exactly like the Post tab (the image container is an inline-block in the figure's centred line instead of a 100%-wide flex box). Selected image: the Alt / Comment / Caption toolbar stays centred above the image, the blue focus ring and resize handles sit on the image, and none of it touches the widget (probe at 1440, 800, 599: toolbar never intersects a widget). Dragging the image's resize handle beside a widget follows the same rule: once the image is wider than the free space it moves below the widget, narrower again and it returns beside (follows from the CSS, not exercised in the prototype). The upload placeholder (500x200) follows the same rule.

A bare top-level becomes a centred block-level box: beside the widget, centred in the free space, if it fits; otherwise below, centred. Legacy

from old posts keeps its inline layout: same beside/below outcome, left-aligned like every legacy inline image. Phones: widget full width, image after it as in any post.
behaviors.drag: Images stay ordinary drop targets: a widget can be dropped just before or just after any image, with no snapping (unlike headings) and no new chip text. If the image is too wide for the free space it shows below the widget after the drop. design:images.rationale: Ronny wants the simpler rule that leaves the author more freedom and looks right at every width. "An image keeps the size you gave it; it sits next to a widget when it fits there, otherwise it starts below the widget" is one sentence, works like text does, never shrinks or stretches anyone's image, and gives authors a real choice: leave an image full size (it goes below the widget, as today) or resize it to put it next to the widget. It is also what the Post tab already does for plain images, so published posts barely change; the work is making the editor match (its 100%-wide flex image container and 100%-wide Excalidraw button pushed every image below) and fixing resized figures, which today are centred on the whole column so the widget eats into them and they drop below even with room to spare. It is consistent with the boxed blocks' "beside if it fits, else below", using the image's own width as the fit test instead of 300px of text. Verified at 15 widths in both views with left/right widgets at 25/33/38/50%, top and bottom aligned, directly after the widget and after a paragraph: zero overlaps, no sideways scroll, identical placement in the editor and the Post tab. Clearing below (B) is just as simple but forbids an image next to a widget even when it obviously fits; shrinking to fit (D) removes the blank strip but overrides the author's size and makes one image change size with the window. Bottom alignment needed a fix in every option: a widget can only line up with a block that runs beside it.

rejected.name: A. No change
rejected.why: Editor and Post tab disagree for small images and diagrams (editor always below, post beside); resized images drop below even when they fit; a bottom-aligned widget followed by an image runs away in the editor.

rejected.name: B. Clears below
rejected.why: Forbids an image next to a widget even when it plainly fits, so small or resized images always leave a blank strip and the author cannot place them beside; drag would have to snap widgets below images; with align=bottom it runs away in the reader too. No better looking than C for full-size images, worse for small ones.

rejected.name: D. Box beside, shrunk to fit (300px floor)
rejected.why: Overrides the author's size: a 1200px screenshot becomes 309px beside a 50% widget and 425px beside 33%, then full width again where the widget stops wrapping, so the same image changes size with the window; the narrow box stays narrow below the widget's end; the reader's bare has no wrapper, so it needs markup changes (the CSS approximation shifted the Post tab in two 1440 shots).

judge:embeds:reader.notes: Verdict: I agree with B (clears below). I checked the designer's final2 shots and metrics: 0 overlaps and no sideways scroll at all 15 widths in both views. The one quote overlap is the quote box, which is invisible beside a right widget and belongs to the quote group. Non-wrapping widths (600/622/520 and below) are unchanged from the baseline (pixel-identical apart from live iframe content). I also ran my own adversarial specimen at 2560, 1440, 760, 640, 599, 560, 400 and 320 in both views: /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-proto/design/embeds/judge-reader/spec.html, shots in /Users/ronnyfernandez/lw-exp3-shots/design/embeds/judge-reader/final/. It covered a tall widget, a paragraph longer than the widget, two embeds in a row, a bottom-aligned widget with a one-line lead, stacked right widgets, Estimaker beside a 50% widget at 599, and an embed before a widget. Results: 0 overlaps, no sideways scroll, and no bottom-align runaway with the CSS stand-in. A paragraph that runs past the widget leaves its embed at normal paragraph spacing (the clear is a no-op there), so there is no leak. YouTube, Metaculus, StrawPoll, Elicit and Calendly all read cleanly below the widget, full width, with the widget's 16px margin above. The editor matches the post: remaining section-height differences are pre-existing (StrawPoll 480 vs 400 or the login box, LW Artifacts 500 vs 525, the editor placing text beside any widget about 18px lower than the post). The editor YouTube parity rule is right, and should become the YouTubeNode code change as proposed. C and D would shrink videos and recreate the narrow fixed-height frames. The holes beside a widget that B leaves are the same cost headings already pay, and the drag chips warn the author. Two reminders. (1) The bottomAlign JS fix is truly required: the CSS stand-in covers only the 'next block is an embed' case. Consider a more general guard as well: if a push does not shrink the gap, there is nothing to align with. That would also catch other blocks that always end below the float. (2) The 'embed inside a container' behavior in the spec is only true until the quote, collapsible and LLM-block rules land, which is the first must-fix.

judge:tables:reader.notes:
Reader lens, all screenshots checked by eye.

What works in the chosen design:
- Short tables pair neatly with a widget on either side (1440 to 560), and editor and post match.
- Tables too wide to fit beside (the 5-column and 7-column tables, the URL table) correctly start below at full width.
- Two widgets on opposite sides work, and bottom alignment with a short table works.
- The editor min-width:0 fix keeps the editor column equal to the post's.
- No overlaps, no sideways scroll.
- No leak: tables that are not beside a widget render the same as baseline (far-table and nowidget are pixel-identical apart from a 1px subpixel shift).
- At widths where widgets don't wrap (600 to 622, 520 and below), nothing changes.

Main disagreement: the designer accepted 'long tables stay narrow beside a widget'. To a reader that is the most visible weakness. The empty area beside a long table (table height minus widget height) is bigger than candidate A's hole beside the widget, and the review table squeezes until words break. The designer rejected the proportional rule for two reasons; neither held up:
- 'Fights bottom alignment': a bottom-aligned widget's frame sits below the table's top, so the measurement skips it. bottom-r33, bottom-para-l33 and bottom-long-r33 were all stable and correct.
- 'Authors can't predict it': the editor shows the same result live; editor and post matched at every width rendered.
The change is one condition in the guard JS the design already needs.

Not real problems:
- Editor and post column splits differ in the specimen only because the editor adds a 92px-per-column colgroup on import. Saved posts would carry it.
- Wide tables run past the column at 360 and 560 in the post only because the harness loads at 1440 and then shrinks the window. A fresh load gets HorizScrollBlock.

Not checkable in the prototype:
- A widget inside a table cell in the post (needs the ContentItemBody fix).
- The real bottomAlign JS fix (the CSS stand-in only matches 7-column tables).

The legacy figure.table rule is nearly dead code, since the editor converts it to a Lexical table on save. Its post rendering looked fine.
